title: Heuristic vs ML tagging experiments - annotator journal
content:
Purpose: quick running notes on comparing hand-coded heuristics vs small supervised taggers for noisy fields (product names, SKU-ish tokens, and mixed alphanumeric IDs).

Status: informal labbook. Not for prime-time. Trying to capture failure modes, small sample eval numbers, and hybrid rules that are cheap to implement in data-cleaning pipelines.

High-level takeaway (so far): heuristics win on high-precision short patterns (currency, simple SKU formats), ML wins on recall for messy natural-language product names and truncated/skipped tokens. But combining them with an adjudication layer (heuristic overrides + ML fallback) gives best upstream label quality with minimal annotator load.

Experiment set-up:
- Small dev eval: 800 examples manually labeled across domains (retail product titles, scraped marketplace listings, support transcripts).
- Models tested: lightweight RoBERTa classifier fine-tuned for token classification (~2–3k labeled tokens), and a few regex/heuristic rulesets (normalized punctuation, parentheses stripping, length heuristics).
- Metrics tracked: precision@span, recall@span, span-F1, delta-to-gold-after-adjudication.

Observed numbers (rough, noisy):
- Heuristics-only: precision 0.92, recall 0.58, F1 0.71
- ML-only: precision 0.81, recall 0.74, F1 0.77
- Heuristics first, ML fallback: precision 0.90, recall 0.78, F1 0.84
(Notes: heuristics tuned aggressively for precision; ML recalls many odd spans that heuristics miss.)

Representative failure cases (examples):
1) Abbreviated titles: "NKE Air Zoom 90s blk/wht sz10"
   - Heuristic: picks up 'NKE' as brand? Sometimes flags as SKU because of uppercase run. Misses the numeric size token as part of product name.
   - ML: captures full title tokens better but sometimes spans the size incorrectly.

2) URLs and trailing IDs: "WidgetPro - model x3000 (ref: wgt-x3000-2022) https://buy.example"
   - Heuristic: removes URL but keeps parentheses group as SKU. Often treats hyphenated ref as SKU when it is part of name.
   - ML: tends to include the ref as spanning the product; sometimes gold says to exclude the ref.

3) Multilingual casing: "Café de Paris - édition limitée"
   - Heuristic: accent stripping breaks token boundaries; classifier handles it but needs unicode normalization during tokenization.

Ruleset ideas that changed outcomes:
- Treat runs of >3 uppercase chars + digits as probable SKU; if preceded/followed by punctuation inside parentheses, downweight as product name.
- If token length <=3 and all-caps, only label as brand if context contains brand markers ("by", "from").
- Strip trailing URLs and email-like tokens before passing to ML; improves precision by ~3–4 points.

Adjudication flow proposal (cheap):
1) Run heuristics first; mark high-confidence spans (confidence tag: HIGHPRECISION).
2) For unresolved tokens / low-confidence heuristics, run ML classifier to propose spans.
3) If heuristic and ML agree -> auto-accept. If conflict -> queue for micro-adjudication or apply tie-breaker rules (e.g., prefer heuristic for short structured tokens, prefer ML for long natural language tokens).

Edgecase catalog (short list):
- Embedded numeric codes inside product descriptors ("soundbar 3000 v2").
- Brand names that are common words ("apple", "windows") – need context signal.
- Organic punctuation: em dashes, slashes used inconsistently in scraped titles.
- Parenthetical translation strings ("(UK)", "(ench)").

Annotator guidance (draft):
- If unsure and span could be SKU, annotate as SKU and add comment; system will surface for adjudication.
- Prefer including measurement/size if it changes consumer meaning ("size 12", "64GB").
- For brands that are lowercased common words, annotate only when explicit brand marker + capitalization pattern present.

Practical implementation notes:
- Pipeline: run normalization (unicode normalize NFKC, collapse whitespace, remove control chars) -> heuristics -> drop urls/iso codes -> classifier -> adjudication.
- Keep an explicit provenance tag per-span (heuristic|ml|adjudicated) for downstream model training and for cost analysis.
- Add a small feedback loop: when annotators correct an ML span, capture that as a training example and retrain nightly for fast iteration.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is the SLA we want for human adjudication? (Immediate for high-traffic tables, batch for long tail) — @Luca to propose.
- Should we persist per-source heuristic overrides (marketplace A uses different SKU format)? Feels necessary.
- How to version remedies so downstream pipelines know why a span was included/excluded (tagging metadata spec).
- Quick UX for micro-adjudication: show heuristic and ML highlight side-by-side. Low-effort prototype in the label tool (see PR above).

Mini action items:
- (Aisha) create a 1000-sample focused eval on electronics titles (ENG-4123) by end of next sprint.
- (Priya) push small normalization library to label-tools PR (#214) — emoji/unicode normalizers.
- (Jon) prototype side-by-side adjudication UI mockups, low fidelity.

Notes to self: capture a few more negative examples where punctuation anchors meaning (colons, pipes), and add a short rule: if token after colon is <4 chars and numeric -> treat as attribute not product.

If anyone picks this up: prioritize creating the small adjudication queue first — it gives highest ROI (fixes noisy long-tail examples quickly) and generates training data for ML fallback.

-- end of scratchpad entry --
